content: Zinc iodide is a chemical compound consisting of zinc and iodine. It appears as a white, granular, and odorless solid that has hygroscopic properties, meaning it absorbs moisture from the atmosphere. Upon absorbing water, it dissolves to form an aqueous solution. At a temperature of 1150°C, zinc iodide vapor undergoes dissociation into its constituent elements, zinc and iodine. This compound is frequently utilized in industrial radiography as an X-ray opaque penetrant. Its primary function in this context is to enhance the contrast between damaged and intact composite materials, thereby improving the accuracy of radiographic imaging. Additionally, zinc iodide is mentioned in United States Patent 4109065, which describes a rechargeable aqueous zinc-halogen cell. This cell incorporates an aqueous electrolytic solution containing a zinc salt, which may include zinc bromide, zinc iodide, or mixtures of these salts. The zinc salt is present in both the positive and negative electrode compartments of the cell, contributing to its electrochemical functionality.
